deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivation. It is a heavily corrected German draft of an official memorandum (Gutachten), written in the first person plural ('Die Unterzeichneten', 'Wir'), addressed to the Royal Hanoverian government ('Königliche Hannoversche Regierung', 'in den hohen Rescripten'). It concerns a proposed geodetic undertaking ('das angeregte Unternehmen') on the figure of the Earth. The previous page discusses the Hanoverian arc measurement, local deflections of the plumb line, and the proposal to measure gravity differences by comparative pendulum observations linked by electric telegraph, after Airy's mean-density-of-the-Earth experiment. The context almost certainly points to J. J. Baeyer's 1861 proposal for a Central European arc measurement ('Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung') and the Hanoverian government's request for advice from Göttingen; this identification is mine and not stated on the page.

The argument of the page, step by step:
(1) The signatories acknowledge the difficulties of combining such works into one investigation. They hold that investigations of the Earth's figure should be left to independent scientific work by individuals once the necessary foundation ('Grundlage') has been supplied. A sentence 'Aber zu dieser Grundlage gehören …' is left unfinished.
(2) How Hanover takes part in producing the new foundation will depend on the outcome of the negotiations.
(3) The second foundation is the determination of astronomical differences of longitude and latitude. Hanover has already done much toward it, as noted in the rescripts. Even independently of the proposed undertaking, the signatories think an extension of this foundation is possible and desirable.
(4) A fragment proposes procuring invariable pendulums ('unveränderliche Pendel', i.e. Kater-type relative-gravity pendulums). These would serve, at the points named in the enclosures, for determinations of longitude differences and gravity differences, apparently 'for a density' determination (reading uncertain).
(5) The text announces a closing summary of the points where Hanoverian cooperation would be feasible and useful; the summary itself is not on this page.

The only implicit scientific content is the standard relative-gravity principle behind the invariable pendulum, which is my addition and not written on the page: for a fixed pendulum, T = 2*pi*sqrt(l/g), so g1/g2 = (T2/T1)^2 and dg/g = -2 dT/T. Telegraphic time comparison gives longitude differences and synchronizes pendulum clocks.

results.what: Administrative/scientific proposal: extend astronomical latitude and longitude determinations, and measure gravity differences at the stations of the Hanoverian arc with invariable pendulums, to study local plumb-line deflections and the figure of the Earth
results.modern_name: Relative gravimetry with invariable pendulums; deflection of the vertical; the Central European Arc Measurement (precursor of the IAG)
results.usually_credited_to: Invariable pendulum: Kater (1818-19). Telegraphic pendulum comparisons: Airy (Harton Colliery, 1854). Central European arc measurement: J. J. Baeyer (1861-62)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of an institutional memorandum on geodetic cooperation with no mathematics. Riemann's participation in a Göttingen expert opinion on the Hanoverian or Central European arc measurement is a minor biographical detail, and it may already be noted in Nachlass catalogues. It contains no mathematical result.

checkable.asserts: Context only, not on the page: for the pendulum period T=2*pi*sqrt(l/g), dT/T = -dg/(2g), the basis of relative gravity measurement with invariable pendulums.

transcription_corrections: 'für die Herstellung derselben … von Hannoverscher Seite sehr geschehen' should most likely read 'schon geschehen'.
In the line 'wissenschaftlichen Arbeit an Einzelnen … werden müssten', the end of the phrase is probably 'Einzelnen überlassen werden müssten'.
'{+Documente[?]+}' above 'Grundlage für die Erreichung dieses Zwecks' is doubtful; it may be part of the insertion 'namentlich'. The reading should stay marked uncertain.
The final fragment 'für ein Dichte[?]' is uncertain; it is possibly 'für die Dichte' (cf. Airy's mean-density experiment on the previous page).
'Von dem Erfolg dieser Verhandlungen wird es abhängen' is correct. The struck line before it may be 'und bis' or 'ad bis'; it is illegible and deleted.
